page0.text:
I'll protect Tohsaka.
Saber isn't dead yet.
Even if Kuzuki was an unexpected monster, Saber still hasn't lost yet.
On top of that, Caster shouldn't be able to finish Saber off.

page1.text:
...
I tighten my grip on the bokutou in my hand.
My eyes lock on Kuzuki to miss not even a blink.
The moment he turns toward Tohsaka, I'll move between them.
Knowing Tohsaka, I'm sure she's going to leap to the side and shoot Kuzuki—

page2.text:
"Ahh...!"
There was no time to take action.
It was in an instant.
The moment I thought Kuzuki's body wavered, he was in front of Tohsaka.

page3.text:
Tohsaka is astonished, but she immediately points her hand at Kuzuki.
And the right hand of the enemy...
The hand that wrecked Saber's neck strikes her in the chest.

page4.text:
"Agh... Guh...!"
Time seems to stop.
All of the air in Tohsaka's lungs goes out from that blow.

page5.text:
This is it.
If a mage can't breathe, they can't cast a spell incantation or carry out most of their abilities.
Though as she just barely managed to leap back, it seems she only had the wind knocked out of her.

page6.text:
But the next attack...
Even though she jumped back, it was only a meter or so.
Such a distance...
...is inconsequential to someone like Kuzuki!

page7.text:
"Khh...!"
I move in between them.
Using my wooden sword as a shield, I plant myself between attacker and prey.
He thrusts his fist.

page8.text:
"Wha...!?"
I can't even see it...!?
How did Saber dodge something like this—
"Agh... Guh...!"
I desperately protect my left side.

page9.text:
A heavy striking sound follows, along with the sound of my sword snapping.
I see Kuzuki coming with his next attack.

page10.text:
I'm going to die.
Instinctively I know it's coming.
The Strengthened wooden sword was the same as steel.
If he can destroy that with one blow, then he can destroy my body no matter where he hits me.

page11.text:
I can't stop him.
Tohsaka is coughing painfully behind me.
I can't see his attacks, and my only weapon was destroyed.

page12.text:
His fist aims precisely for my temple.
Shirou Emiya will die from that hammer-like blow.

page13.text:
I'll die if I don't stop it.
A weapon.
I'm no match for him.
I need a strong weapon to make up for the difference in our strength.

page14.text:
It closes in on my brain.
I imagine myself dying.
No. If that happens...

page15.text:
I will end up dead if I can't stop it.
A weapon. I need a weapon.
A weapon that won't get destroyed by him. Not a wooden sword taken in haste, but a proven, strong weapon.
An extraordinary weapon beyond my ken, yeah, like the ones he uses—

page16.text:
"...Trace, on (Projection, start)."
Then I'll make them. I'll make them even if it's impossible. I'll make them at any cost.
Strengthening and reproducing, something that does exist and something that doesn't...I'll force myself to believe that they're exactly the same.

page17.text:
I don't have time. I can't overthink it. Fake it no matter what.
I don't care if I break or lose something in the process, faster, I don't care if it's fake, hurry, forget it all, I'm not the only life at stake here, if I don't hurry, if I can't stop it, Tohsaka will...!!!

page18.text:
"Huh? No way...!?"
A sight beyond hope.
Tohsaka speaks for me.

page19.text:
"Nnng..."
A muffled voice.
Was that Kuzuki?
Something might've happened to my ears; I can't hear properly.

page20.text:
No, not just my ears, but the sensation in my limbs is numb.
Only my right eye is functioning adequately.
I see Kuzuki's approaching fist.
It's like watching someone else block it.

page21.text:
...
My arms feel hollow.
I don't have any sensation in them, but I swear I can hear my nerves fraying.

page22.text:
His twin swords are in my hands.
The Yang Kanshou and Yin Bakuya.
The name of the swords.
Even though they were reproduced haphazardly, the swords still present themselves to their owner.

page23.text:
But, I'm sorry.
I can't Project you perfectly with my skills.

page25.text:
We spring apart.
The twin swords that parried thirty strikes shatter, as if to say they can't take anymore.
It's not because they lost to Kuzuki's fists.
The twin swords disappeared because I couldn't maintain my image of them.

page26.text:
...
The twin swords must've been unexpected, as Kuzuki shows hesitation for the first time.
Then...
A strong wind stirs up in the intersection.

page27.text:
"Saber...!"
I look toward the wall.
Saber must've recovered, as she stands.
Caster, in front of her, rapidly steps back.

page28.text:
...Yes, that's why it was a mistake.
Just because she was defeated, it didn't mean that she lost her powers. So there's no way Saber, with strong Magic Resistance, could be cornered by Caster.
It's Kuzuki's role to finish Saber off.
Despite that, Caster made a mistake.
She seemed to be planning something, but that excessiveness cost her the chance of victory.

page29.text:
...
Kuzuki retreats.
He stands protective of Caster and as a ward against Saber.
"This is it. We'll retreat, Caster."
He makes an apt decision.

page30.text:
"Master...!? No, Saber is injured. You should be able to defeat her again like before!"
"She is not someone who will fall for it twice. I am the one who underestimated her.
I should have struck her once more."

page31.text:
...Kuzuki is correct.
Saber was cornered because Kuzuki's attacks were unnatural.
But that was before.
I wouldn't be able to deal with them no matter how many times I saw them, but Saber is already used to them.

page32.text:
Tactics are supposed to be unknown to an opponent.
Kuzuki's attacks are powerful, but since they are so unique, their exposure renders future attacks followable.
The first strike must be fatal.
The difference between skills that have been polished to an art form,
and a single move that has been trained to the utmost limits.

page33.text:
"...I understand, Souichirou.
Yes, as long as I am a Servant, I must obey my Master's order."
Who was that directed to?
She spits in disgust and flutters her robe dramatically.

page34.text:
...There is nothing after that.
After the indigo robe wraps around Kuzuki's body, they vanish from the intersection like magic.
